record.paper_title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Randomized rounding appears to work very well for computing low-rank approximations. What are the precise limits and valid operating regimes of this approach for such approximation problems?

evidence.quote: Problem 15 Randomized rounding [1] seems to work very well for computing low-rank approximations. What are the boundaries of this approach?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be a (possibly large) real matrix and let $k$ be a target rank with $1 \le k \le \min(m,n)$. For a probability distribution $p = (p_{ij})$ on the entries of $A$ (or, more generally, a sampling/sketching distribution on rows, columns, or linear measurements), a randomized rounding scheme produces a sparsified or sketched matrix $\widetilde{A}$ from which a rank-$k$ approximation $A_k^{\mathrm{rand}}$ is computed (for example by truncated SVD of $\widetilde{A}$, by projecting $A$ onto a sampled column subspace, or by a Gaussian/sub-Gaussian sketch followed by deterministic rank-$k$ truncation).

Compare $A_k^{\mathrm{rand}}$ to the best rank-$k$ approximation $A_k = \arg\min_{\mathrm{rank}(B)\le k} \|A-B\|$ (in spectral or Frobenius norm). Determine the precise limits and valid operating regimes of randomized rounding as a method for low-rank approximation. Specifically:

(a) Characterize, as a function of the matrix parameters (dimensions $m,n$, target rank $k$, spectral decay of $A$, coherence/incoherence, sparsity, stable rank), the sharp threshold on the sketch size or number of sampled entries needed so that
$$\|A - A_k^{\mathrm{rand}}\| \le (1+\varepsilon)\,\|A - A_k\|$$
holds with high probability, and prove matching lower bounds showing the regime cannot be extended further.

(b) Identify those classes of matrices $A$ and sampling distributions $p$ for which randomized rounding provably fails (in the sense that no choice of sketch size below a problem-dependent barrier achieves the $(1+\varepsilon)$-relative-error guarantee), and quantify these failure regimes.

(c) Delineate the boundary of validity in the presence of finite-precision arithmetic: determine the precision (or condition-number) regimes in which the randomized error analysis remains dominant over deterministic rounding error.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: sharp performance bounds, matching lower bounds for Gaussian and sub-Gaussian sketches, analyses beyond Gaussian distributions (sub-Gaussian entries/columns, bounded columns, bounded-second-moment columns), and finite-precision/mixed-precision rounding-error analyses have all appeared. However, fully characterizing the precise limits across all sampling schemes, matrix classes, and arithmetic precision regimes remains an active research area rather than a single closed result, so the question is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Randomized algorithms for low-rank matrix approximation: Design, analysis, and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys modern randomized SVD, subspace iteration, and block Krylov methods with precise error bounds.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art error analyses for randomized low-rank approximation exist with tight upper bounds.

status_evidence.title: Randomized Low-Rank Approximations beyond Gaussian Random Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Extends analysis to sub-Gaussian entries/columns, bounded columns, and bounded second moment columns, giving minimal sample sizes and error bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Limits of randomized sketching are known across several non-Gaussian distribution classes.

status_evidence.title: Randomized Algorithms for Low-Rank Matrix Factorizations: Sharp Performance Bounds
status_evidence.snippet: Provides theoretical guarantees and lower bounds showing upper bounds are tight.
status_evidence.claim: Matching lower bounds confirming tightness exist in important regimes.

status_evidence.title: Randomized Low Rank Matrix Approximation: Rounding Error Analysis and a Mixed Precision Algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes finite-precision rounding errors that can dominate randomized approximation error in low precision.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-precision boundaries of randomized rounding for low-rank approximation are being characterized.
